editorial:
Imagine you are spending a quiet summer trip in the beautiful mountains of Montana back in 1967. Everything feels peaceful until you realize you are not alone in the woods. You will follow a group of hikers and local rangers who find themselves hunted by something huge and hungry. The vibe is super tense from the start because the movie uses a true story about two separate bear attacks on the same night. It makes you feel like nowhere is safe, and the way the movie builds up the danger will have you gripping your seat. 

What really works here is how the movie doesn't rely on cheap jumpscares. Instead, it focuses on the panic of being chased through the brush. The acting feels real, and the pacing keeps you moving right along with the characters. One downside is that some of the slow parts in the middle might feel a bit long, but the payoff is worth it. If you have a big screen, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see the scenery. If you love owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a great call.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a final, bloody fight between the main survivor and the second bear. After a long chase, the survivor uses a flare to scare the beast away, but only after losing their best friend. The big twist is that the two bears were actually a mother and her cub, which explains why they were so aggressive. It wraps up with a somber look at the real-life victims of the 1967 attacks.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves survival stories and animal horror.
